review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: Nowadays, some people believe that school should reward students who achieve the best academic results, while others argue that greater importance should be placed on students who show significant improvement. Personally, I believe that both outstanding academic performance and personal progress deserve recognition.

Admittedly, rewarding students who have diligently themselves to their studies deserve to their praises and privileges, this may encourage these students and others to strive for further achievements, thereby propelling them towards greater overall academic gains. This kind of competition can be seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best performing individuals are rewarded. Students are used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, enabling them to achieve success later in life.

While academic achievement should certainly be recognised, I also believe that rewarding students who show significant improvement is equally important. Only a few high-achieving students can come first and receive rewards, which may cause others to feel that their efforts are futile because they cant surpass those outstanding individuals. As a result, they may be prone to feeling overwhelmed, disheartened and gradually lose the incentive to study. Furthermore, emphasising improvement can encourage students to be diligent in their studies and help them understand that they need to constantly improve themselves, irrespective of how well they have been performing. This constant desire to outdo themselves can foster a stronger determination to learn and develop rather than simply competing against all others.

In conclusion, although rewarding students with the best academic result can motivate them to strive for excellence, recognising those who make significant progress is equally important. Therefore, I believe that schools should acknowledge both outstanding achievement and individual improvement.

review.overall: Em trả lời đủ bốn phần với lập trường nhất quán và diễn đạt khá chủ động. Body 2 nối được nhóm không nhận thưởng với cảm giác nản, rồi chuyển sang giá trị của việc tự cải thiện; kết luận chốt đúng cả hai nhóm. Tuy nhiên, câu mở Body 1 'rewarding students who have diligently themselves ... deserve' thiếu động từ và chồng hai chủ ngữ, còn 'cant' trái văn phong học thuật. Đây là lỗi đáng sửa nghiêm túc vì nằm ngay câu chủ đề và câu lý do chính, nhưng các đoạn còn lại nhìn chung có mạch. Em cần viết lại Body 1 và tự soát những câu dài trước khi nộp. Body 1 đã được nhận xét lỗi câu mở, nhưng bản chấm cũ vẫn đánh dấu chuyển ý Đạt: câu đầu gộp chính sách thưởng với công sức, còn lý do cạnh tranh vào bằng “This kind” chưa rõ quan hệ bổ sung. Body 2 có “Furthermore” đúng cho lý do thứ hai, nhưng lý do đầu về nhóm khác nản chưa được báo rõ.

review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: Some people believe that parents should take responsibility for education their children at home rather than sending theirs to school. Personally, I am of the opinion that although home schooling offers certain benefits, its disadvantages considerably outweigh its advantages.

On the one hand, proponents of homeschooling argue that this form of education offers notable benefits. First, it allows parents to save money, as they don't have to pay school fees or other school-related expenses are required. Second, children educated at home are less likely to experience bullying and peer pressure, both of which can cause emotional and psychological problems. Finally, parents can teach their children at home by themselves: they can tailor their curriculum and pedagogical approaches to their children's individual needs, abilities and learning pace. This level of personalised education is often not the case in traditional schools due to large class sizes.

On the other hand, the benefits may be outweighed by several significant drawbacks. First, this education approach doesn't necessarily save money, as parents may have to spend a considerable amount of laboratory equipment and private tutors. Moreover, one parent may need to give up their job to cater to their children's academic and personal needs, resulting in a loss of household income. Second, most parents are not well-versed in all school subject, which may make it difficult for them to explain complex concepts effectively and ultimately lead to academic problems. Finally, homeschooling may deprive children of opportunities to develop social skills. Even social problems that children have to faced with at school, such as dealing with bullying or navigating romantic feelings, can help children learn how to handle interpersonal relationships and prepare them for social interactions and workplace situations in the future.
In conclusion, I'm firmly convinced that despite the financial of home-schooling, its disadvantages, particularly the potential academic difficult, considerably outweigh its advantages.
review.overall: Em viết đủ hai phía, quy ba lợi ích cho proponents và giữ kết luận hại hơn lợi. Nhiều câu Body 1 của em đã rõ và đúng, nhất là nhánh cá nhân hóa việc học. Cần sửa các lỗi hình thái và giới từ cụ thể: for educating, spend an amount on equipment, school subjects và have to face. Cụm financial ở kết chưa có danh từ đọc chắc; nếu em muốn nhắc ý miễn học phí, hãy viết rõ financial benefits để người đọc hiểu đúng.

paragraphs: Some people believe that parents should take responsibility for educating their children at home rather than sending them to school. Personally, I am of the opinion that although homeschooling offers certain benefits, its disadvantages considerably outweigh its advantages.

On the one hand, proponents of homeschooling argue that this form of education offers notable benefits. First, it allows parents to save money, as they do not have to pay school fees or other school-related expenses. Second, children educated at home are less likely to experience bullying and peer pressure, both of which can cause emotional and psychological problems. Finally, parents can teach their children at home by themselves: they can tailor their curriculum and pedagogical approaches to their children's individual needs, abilities and learning pace. This level of personalised education is often not the case in traditional schools due to large class sizes.

On the other hand, the benefits may be outweighed by several significant drawbacks. First, this educational approach does not necessarily save money, as parents may have to spend a considerable amount on laboratory equipment and private tutors. Moreover, one parent may need to give up their job to cater to their children's academic and personal needs, resulting in a loss of household income. Second, most parents are not well-versed in every school subject, which may make it difficult for them to explain complex concepts effectively and ultimately lead to academic problems. Finally, homeschooling may deprive children of opportunities to develop social skills. Even social problems that children have to face at school, such as dealing with bullying or navigating romantic feelings, can help children learn how to handle interpersonal relationships and prepare them for social interactions and workplace situations in the future.

In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that despite the potential financial benefits of homeschooling, its disadvantages, particularly the potential academic difficulties, considerably outweigh its advantages.

task.text: In some countries, parents are choosing to teach children themselves at home instead of sending them to school. Do the advantages of homeschooling outweigh the disadvantages?
